New fixes are arriving all the time, and today Google just shared word of a big wave of updates arriving for the company’s hardware. title: Google brings richer document editing to Gemini on mobile and the web
summary: Gemini is ready for your revision notes as its document powers expand.
body: TL;DR Gemini is bringing in-app document editing and preview to mobile and the web. After creating custom files, Gemini users can directly interact with the preview to deliver further revision requests. The mobile app supports PDFs, while Gemini on the web can handle a larger variety of file types. At this point, we’ve all seen how easy it is for AI to generate some documents . But there’s still often a big gap between getting that first draft produced, and fine-tuning the model’s output to the point where every last element is just how we want it to be. Google’s always working on tweaks to improve that process, and today the company shares some of its latest progress. Over on its news blog , Google is highlighting some of the new ways Gemini is learning to work with files like PDFs, spreadsheets, presentations, and even code. Users can now easily explain their edits to Gemini and get previews straight away, combining text and visual input to refine what Gemini creates.

summary: Some lucky users are reportedly receiving the Pixel 11 Pro Fold as a replacement.
body: TL;DR A couple of Pixel 9 Pro Fold owners have received a Pixel 11 Pro Fold as a replacement after hardware issues. This appears to be part of a wider Pixel 9 Pro Fold bug, with issues ranging from a non-functional display to dead front cameras. It’s hard to gauge how severe this problem is right now, but it may be wise to contact Google support if your Pixel 9 Pro Fold is facing similar trouble. Regardless of which Android smartphone you get, it can run into problems over its lifetime. In some cases, the severity of the issue can prompt manufacturers to offer a full replacement. But what happens when there’s no replacement device available? Well, a Pixel 9 Pro Fold user has just found out. According to a user on Reddit , their 256GB Pixel 9 Pro Fold “suddenly developed an issue with the front cameras.” After reaching out to Google support for a solution, the company appears to have approved a 512GB Pixel 11 Pro Fold as the replacement.

title: Garmin Messenger is placing too much trust in SMS verification, and this might not end well
summary: Your old chats might not be gone when your phone number is reassigned.
body: TL;DR A Garmin Messenger user reports restoring their entire chat history on a second phone using only SMS verification, without a Garmin account password. The findings raise concerns that recycled phone numbers could let new owners access previous conversations, including sensitive location information. Garmin has reportedly been informed of the issue, but it hasn’t confirmed a fix. Handing over an old phone number shouldn’t mean handing over your private conversations. But a Garmin Messenger user has raised an uncomfortable question: Could the next person assigned your number inherit your chats, too? In a Reddit post , the user describes installing Garmin Messenger on a second, freshly set-up phone. They entered their existing number, verified an SMS code, and watched their previous conversations reappear. No Garmin account password was required. The second phone reportedly also began sending and receiving messages, with no obvious way to view or remotely disconnect other sessions.

body: TL;DR The Amazon Echo Time $200 camera-free smart alarm clock is available today. It has sleep detection that wakes you within 10 to 60 minutes of a set alarm time. There is a version for kids that has parent-controlled sleep schedules. Amazon is expanding its smart home devices today, updating some existing ones, and adding something completely new with the Amazon Echo Time. The orb-like smart clock is similar in look to the Echo Spot , and with sleep wellness as its focus, it’s meant for the nightstand. As Amazon explains , the Echo Time is powered by Alexa+, and has “science-backed wind-down and wake-up features” that have been given the National Sleep Foundation’s SleepMark designation for meeting evidence-based sleep health standards. Those include a smart alarm that kicks in within 10 to 60 minutes of a set alarm to wake you up when it detects you’re in a lighter sleep. The Echo Time display brightens as it prepares to wake you, and plays a customizable alarm tone that starts quietly and gradually gets louder every time it’s snoozed, up to four times. At night, the display dims and is limited to just the current time or the time of the next set alarm.

The feature will start rolling out in November to users in South Korea. Sleep apnea detection has long been a feature on Samsung’s wearables. Watches as old as the Galaxy Watch 4 have offered sleep apnea detection, and the Galaxy Ring became the first FDA-cleared ring device for sleep apnea detection earlier this year. However, the company is now introducing a new, more advanced function that could prove helpful beyond just detecting signs of sleep apnea. Samsung has announced that it received clearance from both the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Korean Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) for the advanced sleep apnea feature.
